pages.text1: Computing power is provided by computers, and computers will adjust energy consumption on demand.
pages.text2: The Module Bus is used to install hardware. Higher tiers have more slots.

pages.text: Every 1T of computing power generates 2HU of heat, but each computer's heat dissipation is limited. Exceeding the limit will cause heat to accumulate and prevent it from operating.$(br)Tier 2 and above computers can use crushed ice, liquid nitrogen, or Frigid Cryotheum for auxiliary cooling, but there is still a limit.$(br)Therefore, the maximum computing power each computer can handle:$(a)20T (Tier 1) $(9)2P (Tier 2) $(d)24P (Tier 3) $(c)700P (Tier 4)

pages.text1: CPUs produce computing power and consume durability while working. Once depleted, they no longer produce computing power.$(br)Computing power provided:$(br)$(a)1T (Tier 1) $(9)5T (Tier 2)$(br)$(d)60T (Tier 3) $(c)675T (Tier 4)
pages.text2: GPUs provide far more computing power than CPUs, but crafting them requires a CPU one tier higher, and their durability is lower than that of CPUs of the same tier.$(br)Computing power provided:$(br)$(a)25T (Tier 1) $(9)375T (Tier 2)$(br)$(d)5P (Tier 3) $(d)700P (Core)

pages.text: RAM sticks provide the local computing power limit. A computer without RAM sticks cannot provide computing power. They also have durability.$(br)Computing power limit:$(br)$(a)2T (Tier 1)$(br)$(9)10T (Tier 2)$(br)$(d)125T (Tier 3)$(br)$(6)1.2P (Tier 4)$(br)$(c)12.5P (Tier 5) $(d)700P (Core)
